subject: Interpretation of "Plot of the LOD scores against the estimated recombination fractions"

messages.author: 269e905d87d26565
messages.subject: Interpretation of "Plot of the LOD scores against the estimated recombination fractions"
parts:
Hello,

I just wanted to check my map (that i got with JoinMap) on R so I used several functions of this tutorial : http://www.rqtl.org/tutorials/geneticmaps.pdf .
I was wondering if someone could help to understand the plot I obtained after using this command  :

> rf <- pull.rf(mapthis)
> lod <- pull.rf(mapthis, what="lod")
> plot(as.numeric(rf), as.numeric(lod), xlab="Recombin
ation fraction", ylab="LOD score")


 

So I have two different maps that I tested and got the plot you can see above. They are really weird compared to the one I saw in the tutorial. I checked other maps that I have and they have a plot that is closer the one in the tutorial but not these two maps.

What does a plot like that mean ?

Thank you for help !

Diana

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Interpretation of "Plot of the LOD scores against the estimated recombination fractions"
parts:
I would guess that you have largely complete genotype data, except that one set of markers is completely missing genotypes on a set of individuals.
For a pair of markers with the larger amount of genotype data, there's a functional relationship between the estimated recombination fraction and the LOD scores.
For a pair of markers where one or the other or both has the smaller amount of genotype data, there's also a functional relationship between rec frac and LOD, but with a given rec frac corresponding to a smaller LOD score.

karl
